content: Minocycline may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection if used for prolonged or repeated periods. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This document does not list all possible side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before starting minocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Minocycline may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Children under 8 years old may be more susceptible to side effects, particularly tooth discoloration. Tooth discoloration has also been observed in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using minocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Minocycline may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine catecholamine levels, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as complete blood count, kidney, or liver function tests) may be conducted while you are taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking expired minocycline can cause serious illness. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
